lines.text: Researchers built an AI that could tell a husky from a wolf. [1] Then they checked what it was actually looking at. [2] It wasn't the animal.

It was looking at the snow. [1] In the training photos, almost every wolf stood in snow... [2] and every husky, on grass. [3] So the AI learned a shortcut: snow means wolf. [4] Show it a husky in the snow... [5] wolf.
This is the golden rule of AI. [1] Garbage in... [2] garbage out. [3] A model can only learn what its data shows it.

So what makes data good? [1] Quantity: enough examples. [2] Quality: correct labels, no junk. [3] Diversity: wolves on grass too, and faces of every skin tone. [4] And freshness... so the world hasn't moved on.
And to catch a cheating AI... [1] we hide some data away. [2] Train on most of it. [3] Tune on a little. [4] And test on photos it has never seen. [5] A surprise exam.

data.question: An AI spots cats perfectly... but only indoors. Which rule did its data break?

lines.text: Your turn, detective. An AI spots cats perfectly... but only indoors. [1] Which rule did its data break? <pause 2> [2] Diversity! It never saw a cat outdoors.

points: Good data: quantity, quality, diversity, freshness
Always test on data it has never seen

lines.text: Case closed. [1] An AI is only as smart as its data. [2] Next: the AI that memorised every answer... and still failed the exam. Follow, so you don't miss it.
